edits.content:
# E01 — Reliability aggregation

- Register `k = 3` and `minCases = 20` in `shared/agent-dev/reliability-fixture.json`.
- Aggregate deterministic fixture trials in `scripts/lib/reliability-aggregation.mjs`.
- Keep incomplete cases (missing, timeout, crash, skip) visible and outside pass denominators.
- Report pass^k, pass@k, flake, anchors, raw counts, gate, and reasons separately.
- Do not alter product defaults, product locks, approval semantics, or automation.

# Reliability aggregation boundary

The aggregation is an internal deterministic oracle for the agent-dev benefit report. It does not exercise a real provider, a human, or model generalization. pass^k means every one of k trials passed; pass@k means at least one trial passed. They are never interchangeable.

Incomplete cases (missing, timeout, crash, or skip) are retained as evidence and excluded from the complete-case denominator. A retry after a first failure records flake and never erases the first failure. Positive anchors must pass every trial and negative anchors must reject every trial. Safety cases require zero skip and zero flake. Fewer than the registered complete-case minimum is `insufficient-sample`, never PASS.

# E01 acceptance record

Implemented deterministic reliability aggregation in the existing agent-dev benefit report. The fixture registers k=3 and a minimum of 20 complete cases. The report retains raw denominators and incomplete cases, and separately reports pass^k, pass@k, flake, anchors, safety checks, gate, and reasons.

The fixture is explicitly a deterministic oracle. It makes no claim about real providers, human users, or model generalization. Product defaults, product locks, approval semantics, and automation were not changed. README files were intentionally unchanged because this is an internal evaluation-report change with no user-visible interface or configuration change.
